new_statements.quote: Le nzakara est un parler à tons. La différence de hauteur de réalisation de sons est pertinente; elle sert ordinairement à distinguer un mot d'un autre, d'où sa valeur sémantique : pi (bière) / pi (se coucher) : bas / haut. Il faut noter que les tons nzakara présentent trois registres : bas, moyen et haut; donc trois tons ponctuels ou simples et deux tons modulés : un montant et un descendant qui sont pertinents.
new_statements.translation: Nzakara is a tone language. The difference in pitch at which sounds are realized is distinctive; it ordinarily serves to distinguish one word from another, hence its semantic value: pi (beer) / pi (to lie down): low / high. Note that Nzakara tones show three registers: low, mid and high; thus three level or simple tones and two contour tones, one rising and one falling, which are distinctive.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nzakara is described as a lexical tone language (three level tones L/M/H plus contour tones) and neither description mentions word stress or accent at all, so no stress placement rule is stated; the same holds for the independent CAR description (ACATBA/Landi 2005, pp. 32-35: tons ponctuels H, M, B and tons modulés HB, BH, MB, all nine level-tone sequences attested on CVCV).
new_statements.exceptions: None concerning stress. On tone: Landi 2005 p. 34 notes contour tones are almost only attested on grammatical/aspectual morphemes and ideophones, and other contours are loans (e.g. Sango) or grammatical.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone on citation forms (minimal pairs, CVCV nouns); nothing said about phrase-level prominence. Ebanda 1990 describes the Bondo-zone (Bas-Uele, DRC) variety from A.N. Tucker's unpublished tables; Landi/ACATBA 2005 describes the Central African Republic variety from fieldwork since 2000.
new_statements.identity_note: Both opened descriptions are of Nzakara proper (nzak1247) but of different varieties: Ebanda 1990 = Bondo zone, Bas-Uele, DRC (from A.N. Tucker's unpublished 'Tabellen van Tucker's Zande'); Landi/ACATBA 2005 = Central African Republic Nzakara (ACATBA Bible-translation project, fieldwork since 2000). Nzakara is treated as a dialect of Zande (zand1248) by Van Bulck, Tucker and Tucker & Bryan; Kamanda 1990 and Ebanda 1990 treat it as a separate 'parler'. Téguédéré 1982 covers the Gàmbu (CAR) dialect and calls the language 'nzakala'.
